walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical Chemistry — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physical Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physical Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: If 50 cm^3 of a 1 mol/dm^3 solution is diluted to 100 cm^3, what is the new concentration?
options: 0.5 mol/dm^3 — the moles stay the same but the volume doubled.
The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.
The new concentration is 0.05 mol/dm^3 because you doubled the volume so you halve the concentration once and shift the decimal too.
The forward reaction stops once the reverse reaction begins.

mcqs.q: Why does first ionisation energy generally increase across a period?
options: Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.
Atoms get bigger across a period, making electrons easier to add but harder to remove.
The new concentration is 2 mol/dm^3 because adding water makes the solution stronger.
Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays roughly constant, so electrons are held more tightly.

mcqs.q: At dynamic equilibrium, what is happening to the reactions?
options: Both reactions stop because the system has reached balance.
The forward reaction stops once the reverse reaction begins.
Forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates; concentrations remain constant.
Atoms across a period have more shells, pulling electrons closer.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Saturated”?
options: Contains only single C–C bonds; cannot add more atoms across a bond.
Complete: alkane + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O. Incomplete: produces CO and soot.
Compound containing only hydrogen and carbon.
Mixture of hydrocarbons (mostly alkanes), separated by fractional distillation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hydrocarbon”?
options: Compound containing only hydrogen and carbon.
Saturated hydrocarbon with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ — all single bonds.
Methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀.
Contains only single C–C bonds; cannot add more atoms across a bond.

Compound containing only hydrogen and carbon.
